title: The Messy Politics of the Democratic Shutdown Deal

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 回想起当年还在黑胶时代夜店里当DJ的日子，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每晚你都要带着300张最珍爱的唱片去上班，把DJ台变成一个流动的、充满美感的50年历史艺术品快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the story of how a small group of Senate Democrats broke from their colleagues,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将讲述一小群参议院民主党人如何背离同僚，

sentences.en: struck a deal with Republicans to end the government shutdown and touched off the latest civil war inside their party.
sentences.zh: 与共和党人达成协议以结束政府关门，并点燃党内最新内战的故事。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleagues, congressional reporter Katie Edmondson and national political correspondent Shane Goldmacher.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事、国会记者凯蒂·埃德蒙森和国家政治记者谢恩·戈德马彻。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, November 11th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月11日，星期二。

sentences.en: Katie, welcome back.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，欢迎回来。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I just want to explain that we're talking to you on Monday afternoon after a head-spinning few days of news that could keep changing after we talk to you.
sentences.zh: 我想先说明一下，我们是在周一下午采访你的，在此之前经历了令人头晕目眩的几天新闻，而且在我们采访结束后情况可能还会继续变化。

sentences.en: And the reason the past few days have been head-spinning is that from the outside, it looked like Democrats were riding really high after last Tuesday's election,
sentences.zh: 过去几天之所以让人眼花缭乱，是因为从局外人的角度来看，民主党人似乎在上周二的选举后气势如虹，

sentences.en: which seemed to ratify their strategy of keeping the federal government shut down as a way of forcing Republicans and President Trump to reckon with these sky-high health care costs.
sentences.zh: 这场选举似乎印证了他们的战略：通过让联邦政府保持关门状态，迫使共和党人和特朗普总统正视极其高昂的医疗保健成本。

sentences.en: In fact, it seemed to be working so well that in the aftermath of that election, Trump declared that the shutdown was being blamed on Republicans and was helping Democrats.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这招似乎奏效得如此之好，以至于选举结束后，特朗普宣称政府关门应该怪共和党人，这对民主党人有利。

sentences.en: He articulated that idea.
sentences.zh: 他明确表达了这种观点。

sentences.en: And then Democrats tossed this entire seemingly winning strategy out of the window.
sentences.zh: 然后，民主党人却把这个看似稳操胜券的全盘战略扔到了九霄云外。

sentences.en: I didn't see that coming.
sentences.zh: 我可没料到这一出。

sentences.en: Well, I think it gave a lot of people a real sense of whiplash, Michael, because as you said, I remember standing outside of Democrats' closed-door meeting on Wednesday,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这让很多人感到一阵真正的晕眩，迈克尔，正如你所说，我记得周三时我站在民主党人闭门会议的门外，

sentences.en: and they came out sounding thrilled by what voters had just done in New Jersey, New York, Virginia,
sentences.zh: 他们走出来时，对选民刚刚在新泽西、纽约、弗吉尼亚的表现感到兴奋不已，

sentences.en: which is to show overwhelmingly that they sided with the Democratic agenda here, which was focused on lowering costs specifically.
sentences.zh: 选民们压倒性地表明他们站在民主党人的议程这边，而该议程的核心正是专门降低成本。

sentences.en: And so we heard from a lot of Democrats, particularly progressive Democrats,
sentences.zh: 因此我们听到许多民主党人，尤其是进步派民主党人表示，

sentences.en: that, look, voters have just vindicated what our strategy is, and they're telling us they want us to keep up the fight.
sentences.zh: 你看，选民刚刚证明了我们战略的正确性，他们在告诉我们希望我们继续战斗。

sentences.en: But I think what was always brewing under the surface, Michael, was that there was this small clutch of centrist Democrats
sentences.zh: 但迈克尔，我认为水面之下一直在酝酿的是，有一小撮温和派民主党人

sentences.en: who have grown really uncomfortable with all of the pain points that have emerged of the shutdown who are looking for some sort of off-ramp.
sentences.zh: 对政府关门所带来的所有痛点感到越来越不安，他们正在寻找某种退路。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A clutch of Democrats who did not believe that the shutdown was the height of Democratic success.
sentences.zh: 这撮民主党人并不认为政府关门就是民主党成功的巅峰。

sentences.en: So tell us who these senators are and what they started to do.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我们这些参议员是谁，他们开始做什么了。

sentences.en: Well, a lot of these senators hail from kind of purple or reddish states.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些参议员大多来自所谓的摇摆州或偏红的州。

sentences.en: A lot of these are senators who really pride themselves on having some sort of bipartisan credentials to their name, pride themselves on working across the aisle.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有很多人都以拥有某种跨党派资历而自豪，以跨党派合作而自豪。

sentences.en: And we're talking about the senators from New Hampshire, Senator June Shaheen and Maggie Hassan.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是来自新罕布什尔州的参议员珍妮·沙heen和玛吉·哈桑。

sentences.en: We're talking about the senators from Nevada, Catherine Cortez Masto and Jackie Rosen.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是来自内华达州的参议员凯瑟琳·科尔特斯·马斯托和杰基·罗森。
zh_words: 凯瑟琳·科尔特斯·马斯托

sentences.en: Angus King of Maine.
sentences.zh: 来自缅因州的安格斯·金。

sentences.en: He's actually an independent, but he caucuses with Democrats.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是一位独立人士，但与民主党人保持党团合作。

sentences.en: John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, of course, someone who frequently finds himself breaking with Democrats these days.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州的约翰·费特曼，当然，他现在经常与民主党人分道扬镳。

sentences.en: We're talking about Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是来自弗吉尼亚州的参议员蒂姆·凯恩。

sentences.en: And finally and importantly, there's Senator Dick Durbin of Illinois, who's actually the number two Democrat.
sentences.zh: 最后同样重要的是，来自伊利诺伊州的参议员迪克·德宾，他其实是民主党二号人物。

sentences.en: He is the party's whip who will not be running for reelection at the end of his term.
sentences.zh: 他是党内的党鞭，任期结束时将不再竞选连任。

sentences.en: And I think one of the conclusions that they all ended up coming to together is that the chief demand that their party had been asking for,
sentences.zh: 我认为他们最终共同得出的结论之一是，他们党派一直以来的核心诉求——

sentences.en: which is for Republicans to vote to extend the Affordable Care Act subsidies that are set to expire at the end of the year, was not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 即要求共和党人投票延长定于年底到期的《平价医疗法案》补贴——是不可能实现的。

sentences.en: It was not in the cards.
sentences.zh: 这根本不在考虑范围内。

sentences.en: And what made them so sure of that with Republicans starting to openly acknowledge that the shutdown was going well for Democrats?
sentences.zh: 既然共和党人已经开始公开承认政府关门对民主党有利，是什么让他们对此如此确信？

sentences.en: That meant them acknowledging that the health care issue was not going well for them.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们承认医疗保健问题对他们自己不利。

sentences.en: And what furthermore made these Senate Democrats comfortable with the idea of giving up on the central rationale for shutting down the government in the first place, health care?
sentences.zh: 此外，是什么让这些参议院民主党人安心放弃当初关闭政府的核心理由——医疗保健呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think most of them saw the writing on the wall, saw the refusal of President Trump to negotiate,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想他们大多看到了大势所趋，看到了特朗普总统拒绝谈判，

sentences.en: saw the refusal of Speaker Mike Johnson over in the House to even commit to holding a vote on the issue.
sentences.zh: 看到了众议院议长迈克·约翰逊甚至不愿承诺就该问题举行投票。

sentences.en: And then on the other side of the coin, they saw all of the pain that has been inflicted on American voters ever since the shutdown began.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他们看到了自政府关门开始以来给美国选民造成的所有痛苦。

sentences.en: And I think the conclusion that they came to was, yes, extending these subsidies is extremely important.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们得出的结论是：是的，延长这些补贴极其重要。

sentences.en: It's a fight worth having.
sentences.zh: 这是一场值得进行的战斗。

sentences.en: However, we don't see an endgame here, and it is now coming at the expense of a lot of working people.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们看不到这里的最终出路，而且它现在正以牺牲许多劳动人民的利益为代价。

sentences.en: And so they begin these quiet discussions amongst themselves, but also with centrist Republicans in the Senate to try to see,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们开始在内部以及与参议院的温和派共和党人进行私下讨论，试图看看：

sentences.en: is there some sort of deal we can broker here that can give us an acceptable off-ramp so that we can vote to reopen the government and end the shutdown?
sentences.zh: 我们能否在这里达成某种协议，给我们提供一个可以接受的退路，这样我们就可以投票重新开放政府并结束关门？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And what kind of negotiation does this clutch of moderate Senate Democrats enter into with Republicans knowing that health care is off the table?
sentences.zh: 在明知医疗保健已被排除在外的情况下，这撮温和派参议院民主党人与共和党人展开了什么样的谈判？

sentences.en: Well, these negotiations essentially center on spending bills, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些谈判本质上围绕着支出法案展开，对吧？

sentences.en: Funding bills to reopen the government.
sentences.zh: 用于重新开放政府的拨款法案。

sentences.en: But what they ultimately really become centered around are these measures that Democrats are pushing for in order to rein in
sentences.zh: 但它们最终真正聚焦的，是民主党人极力推动的这些措施，旨在遏制

sentences.en: some of the actions taken by the Trump administration during the shutdown and also to protect some of the programs that the White House sought to weaponize during that funding lapse.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府在政府关门期间采取的一些行动，并保护白宫试图在拨款失效期间当作武器的一些项目。

sentences.en: Such as?
sentences.zh: 比如？

sentences.en: Some of the big provisions here include a measure saying all of the workers who were fired or laid off during the shutdown have to be returned to their jobs.
sentences.zh: 这里的一些重大条款包括一项规定：在政府关门期间被解雇或裁员的所有工人都必须重返工作岗位。

sentences.en: Michael,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，

sentences.en: you'll remember that President Trump has hinted repeatedly during the shutdown that maybe he would not give back pay to federal workers who were furloughed during the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，特朗普总统在政府关门期间曾多次暗示，他可能不会向在关门期间被迫休假的联邦员工支付补发工资。

sentences.en: So they include a provision that says the federal government will repay federal workers for the paychecks that they missed and we're providing you with the money to do it right here in this bill.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们包含了一项条款，规定联邦政府将向联邦员工偿还他们错过的薪水，并且我们就在这项法案中为你提供这样做的资金。

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And this gets kind of wonky, but they move to protect this independent agency called the Government Accountability Office.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点繁琐，但他们着手保护一个名为政府问责局的独立机构。

sentences.en: And this is a government agency that essentially is a watchdog for how the White House handles the funds that Congress appropriates.
sentences.zh: 这是一个基本上负责监督白宫如何处理国会拨款资金的政府机构。

sentences.en: This is an agency that has blown the whistle on the White House seven times alone this year, saying that the White House has illegally handled money that Congress appropriated.
sentences.zh: 仅今年一年，该机构就曾七次向白宫发出警告，称白宫非法处理了国会拨款的资金。

sentences.en: And this is an agency that actually has the power to sue the White House over impoundment or when the White House refuses to release funds that Congress has appropriated.
sentences.zh: 并且该机构实际上有权就扣留资金或白宫拒绝释放国会拨款资金的事宜起诉白宫。

sentences.en: And so House Republicans had pushed to essentially gut the budget of that agency and to also revoke its power to sue the White House.
sentences.zh: 因此，众议院共和党人此前一直推动实质性削减该机构的预算，并剥夺其起诉白宫的权力。

sentences.en: And so in these negotiations, the senators say, if you want our vote to reopen the government, you need to make sure that this agency is safe, essentially,
sentences.zh: 所以在这些谈判中，参议员们表示：如果你需要我们的投票来重新开放政府，你必须确保这个机构基本上是安全的，

sentences.en: that it has the budget that it needs.
sentences.zh: 它拥有所需的预算。

sentences.en: And it retains all of the powers that it currently has in order to sue the White House.
sentences.zh: 并且它保留目前拥有的所有权力，以便能够起诉白宫。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: And on health care, of course, the senators know that they cannot get a guarantee on a vote.
sentences.zh: 当然，在医疗保健方面，参议员们知道他们无法获得投票的保证。

sentences.en: But they do get this promise from Senator John Thune of South Dakota, the majority leader, that he will hold a vote later in December,
sentences.zh: 但他们确实从南达科他州参议员、多数党领袖约翰·图恩那里得到了承诺，即他将在12月晚些时候举行投票，

sentences.en: an up or down vote on whether or not Republicans will extend the ACA tax subsidies.
sentences.zh: 就共和党人是否会延长平价医疗法案税收补贴进行赞成或反对的投票。

sentences.en: So in short,
sentences.zh: 简而言之，

sentences.en: these Democrats negotiate a deal that pretty much undoes a lot of the damage from the shutdown and preserves this government accountability office that matters to them as an institution that keeps the president in check.
sentences.zh: 这些民主党人谈判达成了一项协议，该协议几乎撤销了政府关门造成的许多损害，并保留了对他们至关重要的政府问责局，作为一个能够制衡总统的机构。

sentences.en: And finally, and it seems somewhat significantly, they get what they see as an ironclad promise that Senate Republicans will vote on renewing Affordable Care Act subsidies,
sentences.zh: 最后，似乎在某种程度上意义重大的是，他们得到了他们认为如铁板钉钉般的承诺：参议院共和党人将对延长《平价医疗法案》补贴进行投票，

sentences.en: which perhaps they don't think Republicans will, but that would put Republicans on record as not doing it.
sentences.zh: 也许他们不认为共和党人会这么做，但这会让共和党人留下不支持该法案的正式记录。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What they want, Michael, is exactly that.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，他们想要的正是这个。

sentences.en: They want to put every single Senate Republican on the record on this issue.
sentences.zh: 他们希望让每一位参议院共和党人都在这个问题上留下正式记录。

sentences.en: And so all of the details of exactly what they had secured started trickling out on Sunday evening.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于他们究竟获得了什么的种种细节在周日晚上开始逐渐流出。

sentences.en: I was sitting up at the Capitol and lo and behold,
sentences.zh: 当时我正坐在国会大厦里，结果就在这时，

sentences.en: the Senate Appropriations Committee starts putting out legislative text that actually contains the details of these policy wins the Democrats had secured.
sentences.zh: 参议院拨款委员会开始发布立法文本，其中实际包含了民主党人所获得的这些政策胜利的细节。

sentences.en: And so I'm kind of tearing through these bills, right, trying to read exactly what's in them.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始仔细研读这些法案，对吧，试图弄清楚里面到底写了什么。

sentences.en: And it becomes very clear the more that you read that it seems like there's really a deal here.
sentences.zh: 越读越清楚地表明，这里似乎真的达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: I think we just have to explain this, Katie, because most of us imagine that Congress is this very top-down place where decisions come from upon high.
sentences.zh: 我想我们必须解释这一点，凯蒂，因为我们大多数人认为国会是一个自上而下的决策地方，决策都来自高层。

sentences.en: But what you're describing is a handful of Senate Democrats, a little bit going seemingly rogue and reaching a deal to try to end the shutdown with Republicans,
sentences.zh: 但你所描述的却是一小撮参议院民主党人，有点像在单干，并与共和党人达成了一项旨在结束政府关门的协议，

sentences.en: and the leadership of the Senate Democrats is not really involved.
sentences.zh: 而参议院民主党领导层实际上并未真正参与其中。

sentences.en: Well, I'm really glad that you brought this up, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很高兴你提出这一点，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I mean, that is completely right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这完全正确。

sentences.en: But typically, and especially in the past couple of years, Congress has been a very top-down institution.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，特别是在过去几年里，国会一直是一个非常自上而下的机构。

sentences.en: What we saw here really was a return to sort of a style of legislating that was more common maybe six years ago, ten years ago.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里看到的，实际上是回归了一种可能在六年前、十年前更为常见的立法风格。

sentences.en: These were the so-called gangs that senators really prided themselves on being a part of, right?
sentences.zh: 这些就是所谓的“帮派”，参议员们曾为自己是其中一员而感到自豪，对吧？

sentences.en: It was the idea that me and my Democratic friends are going to sit down in a closed-door room with you and your five Republican friends,
sentences.zh: 这是一种这样的理念：我和我的民主党同僚将和你的五位共和党同僚坐在一间闭门会议室里，

sentences.en: and we're going to hammer this out amongst ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们将在内部自己把这个问题敲定。

sentences.en: And that's really what we saw here, and I think it's one of the reasons why, again, their sudden declaration that they had a deal really did surprise a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这确实就是我们在这里看到的，我认为这也是为什么他们的突然宣布——他们达成了一项协议——确实让许多人感到惊讶的原因之一。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And, Michael, the other surprising thing about the Senate is that even though it is known for being such a slow-moving institution,
sentences.zh: 而且，迈克尔，关于参议院另一个令人惊讶的事情是，尽管它以行动迟缓著称，

sentences.en: it can really move quickly when its leaders want it to.
sentences.zh: 但当其领导人希望它行动时，它可以行动得非常快。

sentences.en: And so it was really not long after these centrist Democrats declared that they had the votes for a compromise to reopen the government that we saw that compromise be put to a vote on the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些温和派民主党人宣布他们拥有重新开放政府的妥协方案所需的票数后不久，我们就看到该妥协方案被提交到参议院大厅进行投票。

sentences.en: And I think this was the moment that the vast majority of us, myself included,
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我们绝大多数人（包括我自己）

sentences.en: got clued in on Sunday night just in time for a news conference in which this small group of Democrats goes up to the microphone and tries to explain why they're doing what they're doing and why,
sentences.zh: 在周日晚上获得消息的时刻，刚好赶上了一场新闻发布会，这小群民主党人走上麦克风前，试图解释他们为什么要这样做，以及为什么

sentences.en: in a sense, they have gone around the rest of their Democratic colleagues.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，他们绕过了其余的民主党同僚。

sentences.en: Can you just talk to us about what they said?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们聊聊他们说了什么吗？

sentences.en: Today, the Senate voted to start reopening the government.
sentences.zh: 今天，参议院投票决定开始重新开放政府。

sentences.en: So shortly after casting their votes, this clutch of Democrats holds a news conference right off the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 因此，在投完票后不久，这撮民主党人在参议院大厅附近举行了一场新闻发布会。

sentences.en: We took a big step forward to protect the health care of tens of millions of Americans in exchange for funding through January 31St.
sentences.zh: 我们迈出了巨大的一步，以换取截至1月31日的拨款，从而保护数千万美国人的医疗保健。

sentences.en: And they talk about how important they believe extending these health care subsidies is.
sentences.zh: 他们谈到了延长这些医疗保健补贴有多么重要。

sentences.en: With the government reopened, we must move quickly to deliver on that promise and to keep health care premiums affordable.
sentences.zh: 随着政府重新开门，我们必须迅速行动，兑现承诺，并保持医疗保险费的负担能力。

sentences.en: But mostly they talk about the pain that people are experiencing in a shutdown.
sentences.zh: 但他们主要谈论的是人们在政府关门期间经历的痛苦。

sentences.en: We were seeing lines to our food banks in northern Nevada.
sentences.zh: 我们在内华达州北部看到了前往食品银行排起的长队。

sentences.en: These were lines that I hadn't seen since the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这些排队的长龙是我自大流行以来从未见过的。

sentences.en: You have senators talking about SNAP recipients, right, who are going hungry.
sentences.zh: 你听到参议员们谈论SNAP（补充营养援助计划）的受益者，对吧，他们正在挨饿。

sentences.en: We have TSA agents.
sentences.zh: 我们有运输安全管理局（TSA）的特工。

sentences.en: We have airport controllers.
sentences.zh: 我们有机场管制员。

sentences.en: You hear about the federal workers who have gone for weeks without a paycheck.
sentences.zh: 你听到了关于那些数周没有拿到薪水的联邦员工的报道。

sentences.en: This agreement ensures that law enforcement, air traffic controllers, and other federal workers get paid.
sentences.zh: 这项协议确保了执法人员、空中交通管制员和其他联邦员工能够拿到薪水。

sentences.en: And one by one, it just becomes very clear that for these senators, continuing on with this shutdown was simply not tenable.
sentences.zh: 而且一个接一个地，情况变得非常清楚，对这些参议员来说，继续让政府关门是根本站不住脚的。

sentences.en: This was the only deal on the table.
sentences.zh: 这是桌面上唯一的协议。

sentences.en: It was our best chance to reopen the government and immediately begin negotiations to extend the ACA tax credits that tens of millions of Americans rely on to keep costs down.
sentences.zh: 这是我们重新开放政府并立即开始谈判以延长数千万美国人依赖的ACA税收抵免以降低成本的最佳机会。

sentences.en: Thank you all.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: Thank you all.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: And yet, as we could tell from what was happening on the floor of the Senate on Sunday night, the vast majority of their Democratic colleagues disagree with them.
sentences.zh: 然而，正如我们从周日晚上参议院大厅发生的事情所能看出的那样，绝大多数民主党同僚并不同意他们的看法。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: At least that's how they voted.
sentences.zh: 至少他们的投票结果是这样体现的。

sentences.en: There were exactly eight Democrats who voted for this deal to reopen the government.
sentences.zh: 恰好有八名民主党人投票赞成这项重新开放政府的协议。

sentences.en: And, Michael, that was the magic number of Democrats needed in order for this deal to advance.
sentences.zh: 而且，迈克尔，那是该协议得以推进所需的民主党人的神奇数字。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Which means that the entire rest of the Democratic caucus voted no.
sentences.zh: 这意味着其余所有的民主党党团成员都投了反对票。

sentences.en: Not only did they vote no, a lot of them were pretty vocal in saying how frustrated they were by this decision made by some of their colleagues.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅投了反对票，其中许多人还非常直言不讳地表达了他们对同僚们做出这一决定的沮丧之情。

sentences.en: Tonight, what this Senate is about to do is make a horrific situation even worse.
sentences.zh: 今晚，参议院即将做的事只会让糟糕的局面雪上加霜。

sentences.en: And you heard this frustration coming from a wide swath of the Democratic caucus.
sentences.zh: 你听到这种沮丧情绪来自民主党党团的广泛阶层。

sentences.en: Progressives like Senator Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 像参议员伯尼·桑德斯这样的进步派人士。

sentences.en: If this vote succeeds, over 20 million Americans are going to see at least a doubling in their premiums in the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 如果这次投票成功，超过2000万美国人的平价医疗法案保费将至少翻倍。

sentences.en: But you also heard similar noises being made by people like Senator Alyssa Slotkin, who I think of as being a pretty moderate Democrat from Michigan,
sentences.zh: 但你也听到类似的声音来自诸如参议员阿丽莎·斯洛特金这样的人，我认为她是一位相当温和的密歇根州民主党人，

sentences.en: who said that she simply couldn't lend her vote to this effort because there was no real health care deal on the table.
sentences.zh: 她表示自己实在无法将选票借给这项努力，因为桌面上根本没有真正的医疗保健协议。

sentences.en: And that's what she wanted for the American people.
sentences.zh: 而这正是她希望为美国人民争取到的。

sentences.en: The Democratic leader, Mr. President, America is in the midst of a Republican-made health care crisis.
sentences.zh: 民主党领袖，议长先生，美国正处于一场由共和党制造的医疗保健危机之中。

sentences.en: And even Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, who is the leader of the Senate Democratic Caucus.
sentences.zh: 甚至连纽约州的参议员查克·舒默，也就是参议院民主党党团的领袖，

sentences.en: I must vote no.
sentences.zh: 我必须投反对票。

sentences.en: Says that he is going to oppose this deal that was brokered by some of his own members.
sentences.zh: 他说他将反对这项由他自己的一些成员斡旋达成的协议。

sentences.en: And he says,
sentences.zh: 并且他说，

sentences.en: This health care crisis is so severe, so urgent, so devastating for families back home that I cannot in good faith support this.
sentences.zh: 这场医疗保健危机如此严重、如此紧迫、对家乡的家庭而言如此具有毁灭性，以至于我无法凭良心支持这一点。

sentences.en: Support this CR that fails to address the health care crisis.
sentences.zh: 支持这个未能解决医疗保健危机的临时拨款法案（CR）。

sentences.en: Now, Michael, it was really only minutes after these centrist Democrats made their declaration that they were ready to vote to reopen the government,
sentences.zh: 好了，迈克尔，就在这些温和派民主党人宣布他们准备投票重新开放政府仅几分钟后，

sentences.en: that Democrats on Capitol Hill were already hearing from their voters all across the country.
sentences.zh: 国会山上的民主党人就已经开始听到来自全国各地选民的声音了。

sentences.en: Actually, as I was standing outside of that closed-door meeting, I looked over at a senior Democratic aide who was scrolling on his phone,
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我站在那场闭门会议外面时，我看到一位资深民主党幕僚正在低头刷手机，

sentences.en: and his face was—he kind of just had a funny look on his face.
sentences.zh: 他的表情——他的脸部神情有点滑稽。

sentences.en: He was almost a little ashen, and I said, well, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 他甚至显得有点面色灰白，我便问，怎么了？

sentences.en: And he said, oh, I'm just looking at the reactions to this on social media.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，我只是在看社交媒体上对此事的反应。

sentences.en: And what he was seeing is what I think we've all seen.
sentences.zh: 而他所看到的，正是我想我们大家都有目共睹的。

sentences.en: What, if anything, did Democrats get out of a 40-plus days of a shutdown?
sentences.zh: 民主党人在长达40多天的政府停摆中，究竟得到了什么，如果有的话？

sentences.en: They didn't get anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么也没得到。

sentences.en: This is the same deal that senators—
sentences.zh: 这就是参议员们达成的同一协议——

sentences.en: On social media, on cable news.
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体上，在有线新闻节目中。

sentences.en: It is unconscionable, unconscionable.
sentences.zh: 这简直丧心病狂，丧心病狂。

sentences.en: This emotionally charged explosion within the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 民主党内部这种情绪激昂的爆发。

sentences.en: Like, why are we acting as if Democrats just lost the election?
sentences.zh: 就像是，我们怎么表现得好像民主党刚输了选举一样？

sentences.en: Democrats had overwhelming victories.
sentences.zh: 民主党取得了压倒性的胜利。

sentences.en: I don't understand how a Democratic senator goes, wow, we won really big.
sentences.zh: 我无法理解为什么会有民主党参议员觉得，哇，我们赢得太棒了。

sentences.en: Let me cave now.
sentences.zh: 现在让我妥协吧。

sentences.en: I don't understand what these people in Washington think they're doing representing the people who they claim to represent.
sentences.zh: 我搞不懂华盛顿的这些人认为他们代表声称要代表的民众时，究竟在搞什么名堂。

sentences.en: That I think has resurrected a lot of the sort of fierce debates that are happening internally within the party when it comes to how should Democrats position themselves in this moment?
sentences.zh: 我认为这重新激化了党内关于“民主党此刻应如何定位自己”的许多激烈内部辩论，

sentences.en: How can Democrats best fight back against the Trump administration?
sentences.zh: 民主党人该如何最好地反击特朗普政府？

sentences.en: Well, Katie, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，凯蒂，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Shane, thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 谢恩，谢谢你能来。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: The last time you were in the studio—
sentences.zh: 你上次来演播室是——

sentences.en: Less than one week ago.
sentences.zh: 不到一周前。

sentences.en: Less than one week ago, election night, and you came on to observe what an extraordinary moment of triumph it was for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 不到一周前，即选举之夜，你当时来是为了观察民主党人取得的这一无比辉煌的胜利时刻。

sentences.en: And now, less than a week later, the Democrats are screaming at each other, and resounding victory at the polls has yielded to claims, as Katie just said, of capitulation,
sentences.zh: 然而现在，不到一周的时间，民主党人却在互相叫嚷，正如凯蒂刚才所说，原本响亮的民调胜利演变成了对屈服、

sentences.en: betrayal, caving.
sentences.zh: 背叛和妥协的指责。

sentences.en: What a difference a week makes.
sentences.zh: 一周的时间能带来多大的改变啊。

sentences.en: And the term that has come up as I've talked to Democratic strategists has been that this feels like a self-own for the Democratic Party,
sentences.zh: 在我与民主党战略人士交谈时，出现这样一个词：他们觉得这简直是民主党在自毁前程，

sentences.en: that the Democratic Party had been riding high after a rough week for Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 在经历了特朗普度过艰难的一周后，民主党本该意气风发。

sentences.en: And here, starting this next week, they decided this was the moment to give up a fight that the party's base had been craving, and one that they seemingly had been winning,
sentences.zh: 而就在这里，从接下来的一周开始，他们决定放弃一场党内基层一直渴望的斗争，而且这场斗争他们似乎本来正在取胜，

sentences.en: at least politically.
sentences.zh: 至少在政治上是这样。

sentences.en: I want you to answer, to the best of your ability, this very simple question.
sentences.zh: 我希望你尽你所能回答这个非常简单的问题。

sentences.en: Taken in its totality, if we assume this shutdown is going to soon be over, was this a good experience for the Democrats or a bad one?
sentences.zh: 综合来看，如果我们假设这次政府停摆很快就会结束，这对民主党来说是一次好的经历还是糟糕的经历？

sentences.en: Let's start with the good.
sentences.zh: 让我们从好的一面开始说起。

sentences.en: The good is that the Democratic Party has clearly elevated two issues that it feels are the winning issues for the party.
sentences.zh: 好的一面是，民主党明确提升了两个他们认为对党内大有胜算的议题。

sentences.en: The first is health care, and the second is affordability told through health care.
sentences.zh: 第一个是医疗保健，第二个是通过医疗保健体现的负担能力。

sentences.en: And those have been the dominant topic of conversation for weeks, which is pretty hard to pull off when you're the minority party with no power in Washington.
sentences.zh: 这些议题连续几周成为讨论的绝对焦点，作为一个在华盛顿没有权力的少数党，这其实是很难做到的。

sentences.en: And it took a shutdown for them to do that and for them to elevate those issues in hopes that long past the shutdown, voters will think, oh,
sentences.zh: 正是政府停摆迫使他们做到了这一点，让他们得以提升这些议题，希望在停摆很久之后，选民们仍会觉得，哦，

sentences.en: that's the party that's actually fighting for me on those issues.
sentences.zh: 那才是真正为我在这些议题上战斗的政党。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's one side of the ledger, the good side.
sentences.zh: 所以这是账本的一面，好的一面。

sentences.en: That's the good side.
sentences.zh: 这就是好的一面。

sentences.en: But the risk of that fight was inflating people's expectations that they were actually going to win something on those issues, right?
sentences.zh: 但这场斗争的风险在于，它抬高了人们的期望，让他们以为自己真的能在这些议题上赢得什么，对吧？

sentences.en: They had to say, we're fighting for this because we want X, Y, Z outcomes.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不说，我们在为之奋斗，因为我们想要X、Y、Z这样的结果。

sentences.en: And they didn't get those outcomes.
sentences.zh: 而他们并没有得到这些结果。

sentences.en: They've got the promise of a vote, which is not guaranteed to pass.
sentences.zh: 他们只得到了一次投票的承诺，这并不能保证一定能通过。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Someone called it a pinky promise.
sentences.zh: 有人称之为拉勾承诺。

sentences.en: A pinky promise.
sentences.zh: 拉勾承诺。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: And so the bad is that the timing of this shutdown ending is coming just as the Democratic Party was actually starting to feel some rare momentum in the Trump era.
sentences.zh: 所以不好的一面在于，这次停摆结束的时机，恰好赶在民主党在特朗普时代开始感受到一些难得的势头之际。

sentences.en: That's exactly when the Democrats chose to cave, seemingly when things were going great.
sentences.zh: 而这正是民主党人选择妥协的时候，似乎正是在局势一片大好之时。

sentences.en: And so this decision to cave at this moment is unleashing the anger and energy that has been herbaling beneath the surface for months,
sentences.zh: 因此，在这个时刻做出妥协的决定，释放了几个月来一直在水面下暗流涌动的愤怒与能量，

sentences.en: which is the Democrats are angry at their own party.
sentences.zh: 那就是民主党人对他们自己的党感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And they have been all year.
sentences.zh: 而且他们一整年都是如此。

sentences.en: They have been basically since Kamala Harris loSt.
sentences.zh: 基本上从卡马拉·哈里斯落败以来就一直是这样。

sentences.en: And the shutdown was this sort of notable little reprieve where Democrats kind of stopped hating Democrats for a little while.
sentences.zh: 这次政府停摆就像是一个值得注意的小喘息，民主党人有那么一会儿停止了互相痛恨。

sentences.en: I mean, there was a Quinnipiac poll over the summer that showed that Democratic approval rating of Democrats in Congress was at 39 percent.
sentences.zh: 我是说，昆尼皮亚克大学夏天的一项民调显示，民主党人对国会民主党人的支持率仅为39%。

sentences.en: That's a really bad stat.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常糟糕的数据。

sentences.en: And that same pollster took a poll in October and it had jumped 20 percentage points to 58 percent.
sentences.zh: 而同一家民调机构在10月份进行了一次民调，支持率跃升了20个百分点，达到58%。

sentences.en: Not great.
sentences.zh: 算不上多好。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: People aren't suddenly in love.
sentences.zh: 人们并不是突然间爱上了他们。

sentences.en: Well, it's a big increase.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个很大的增幅。

sentences.en: I'll be really interested to see what those numbers look like now that that bubble of hope had been inflated and deflated in this shutdown.
sentences.zh: 我很想看看，随着这次停摆中那串充满希望的泡沫被吹大又被戳破，现在的这些数字会是什么样子。

sentences.en: Well, talk about the consequences of having created this hope bubble, this idea that the shutdown was going to lead to meaningful changes in the country's health care system,
sentences.zh: 那么，谈谈制造这个“希望泡沫”的后果吧，即政府停摆将给国家医疗体系带来实质性改变的这种想法，

sentences.en: which we don't think they are.
sentences.zh: 而我们认为这并不会发生。

sentences.en: And in a broader sense would show that Democrats were willing to really take on the president, which they were until they weren't.
sentences.zh: 从更广泛的意义上讲，这也表明民主党人愿意真正与总统硬刚，他们确实这样做了，直到他们不再这样做为止。

sentences.en: I mean, this was always the risk of entering the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这历来就是陷入政府停摆的风险所在。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Chuck Schumer was very clear about why they should have this shutdown, what they were fighting for.
sentences.zh: 查克·舒默对为什么要进行这次停摆、他们在为什么而战一直非常明确。

sentences.en: But there wasn't an endgame to get out of it with a win on policy.
sentences.zh: 但并没有一个能通过政策胜利来收场的终局计划。

sentences.en: And so you were always going to have this ugly ending, as people have described it to me, that the fear of how it was going to end was going to be bad,
sentences.zh: 所以正如人们对我说的那样，你注定会迎来一个丑陋的结局，这种对结局会很糟糕的恐惧，

sentences.en: even if in all these unlikely ways they were actually doing OK in public polling about the issue.
sentences.zh: 即便他们在所有这些不太可能的情况下，在有关该议题的民调中其实表现得还不错。

sentences.en: And so who actually voted to end the shutdown, I think, is really revealing.
sentences.zh: 因此，究竟是谁投票结束了停摆，我认为这非常有启示意义。

sentences.en: And the people who voted to actually end the shutdown are the people furthest removed from facing any real backlash because none of those eight Democratic senators,
sentences.zh: 那些真正投票结束停摆的人，是距离面临任何真正强烈反对最远的人，因为那八位民主党参议员，

sentences.en: Democratic-aligned senators, are on the ballot next year.
sentences.zh: 即亲民主党的参议员，明年都不用参加选票选举。

sentences.en: They're all either retiring or on the ballot in 2028 or 2030.
sentences.zh: 他们要么即将退休，要么在2028年或2030年才面临选举。

sentences.en: The Senate has these staggered terms, and this is something you can do in Washington.
sentences.zh: 参议员实行错位任期制，这是你在华盛顿可以做到的一点。

sentences.en: Try to keep your most vulnerable people out of having to cast the toughest votes.
sentences.zh: 尽量让你最脆弱的成员免于投下最艰难的选票。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: You're saying that the Democrats, to the degree that this is any kind of organized strategy, which I guess we're not entirely sure, put the safest Democratic senators,
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，民主党人——如果这可以算作某种有组织策略的话，虽然我想我们对此并不完全确定——让那些最安全、

sentences.en: furthest from election, out to do the quote-unquote dirty work here of reopening the government without fulfilling the promise of improving health care.
sentences.zh: 距离选举最远的民主党参议员出来，在这里做所谓“不光彩的工作”，在未能兑现改善医保承诺的情况下重启政府？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think the yes votes here are really revealing.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这里的赞成票真的很有启发性。

sentences.en: But there's one no vote that I found especially interesting.
sentences.zh: 但有一个反对票我觉得特别有意思。

sentences.en: Who?
sentences.zh: 谁？

sentences.en: So, John Ossoff, he is the most vulnerable senator up for election next year.
sentences.zh: 约翰·奥索夫，他是明年面临选举的最脆弱的参议员。

sentences.en: So he will face the voters.
sentences.zh: 所以他将直面选民。

sentences.en: And he's running in Georgia and really focused on his general election, right?
sentences.zh: 他正在佐治亚州参选，并且全神贯注于他的大选，对吧？

sentences.en: No one's running against him in the primary right now.
sentences.zh: 目前党内初选里没有人跟他竞争。

sentences.en: And what the no vote here says is that he doesn't want to risk backlash from inside his own party in this campaign,
sentences.zh: 这里投反对票的意思是，他不想在这场竞选中冒着遭到党内强烈反对的风险，

sentences.en: whether that's from a potential primary challenger who could get recruited from one of these angry groups, or whether it's the small donors who are fueling his campaign deciding,
sentences.zh: 无论是来自可能被这些愤怒群体招募的潜在初选挑战者，还是来自资助其竞选的小额捐赠者，他们可能会想，

sentences.en: you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Maybe we're not so into John Ossoff.
sentences.zh: 也许我们没那么支持约翰·奥索夫了。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to risk backlash.
sentences.zh: 他不想冒引发强烈反对的风险。

sentences.en: That's fascinating, because as you're suggesting, John Ossoff could reasonably be most focused on a Republican opponent in a general election saying,
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了，因为正如你所暗示的，约翰·奥索夫本可以合乎逻辑地把最大精力放在大选中对付共和党对手上，对方会说，

sentences.en: you should have voted to reopen the government.
sentences.zh: 你本该投票重启政府。

sentences.en: That's what matters in this race.
sentences.zh: 这才是这场竞选的关键所在。

sentences.en: And instead, what you're saying is he's more worried about upsetting Democrats in a potential primary, and that's what animated his vote on the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 相反，你的意思是他在初选中更担心惹恼民主党人，正是这一点左右了他对政府停摆的投票。

sentences.en: And in the end, he votes to keep the government shut down because he wants to look like he's on the side of the Democratic base.
sentences.zh: 最后，他投票支持维持政府停摆，因为他想显得自己站在民主党基层这一边。

sentences.en: That's what we think happened here.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们认为发生的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, I have not talked to Senator Ossoff here, but what you can see is that there are two choices.
sentences.zh: 是的，我没有跟奥索夫参议员交谈过，但你可以看到这里有两种选择。

sentences.en: Choice one is vote to reopen the government and say, I'm going to buck my party and I'm going to reopen the government, even if people on my left attack me for it.
sentences.zh: 选择一是投票重启政府，然后说，我要顶住党内的压力重启政府，哪怕我左翼的人因此攻击我。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's a selling point in a lot of places.
sentences.zh: 在很多地方，这都是一个卖点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so here's a Democrat saying, you know, that's not the right calculus here to the extent he's making a politically motivated choice.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一位民主党人在说，你知道，如果他是从政治动机出发做出选择的话，这并不是正确的算计。

sentences.en: The right calculus is to make sure that your own party likes you and supports you and sees you as a fighter because you want that energy behind you in a coming midterm election.
sentences.zh: 正确的算计是确保你自己的党喜欢你、支持你，并视你为主心骨，因为你希望在即将到来的中期选举中有这股能量为你撑腰。

sentences.en: I noticed as well that several of the Democrats hoping to be the next presidential nominee woke up this morning on Monday and decided that this was a terrible decision.
sentences.zh: 我也注意到，几位渴望成为下一任总统候选人的民主党人在今天周一醒来后，认为这是一个糟糕的决定。

sentences.en: I think a lot of them decided last night they didn't even wait.
sentences.zh: 我想他们中的很多人昨晚就已经决定了，甚至都没等。

sentences.en: You know, like they started issuing these statements on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如他们在周日就开始发表这些声明。

sentences.en: You saw it from Gavin Newsom, who said just as it was done, that America deserves better.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到加文·纽森的表态，他刚一结束就说，美国值得拥有更好的。

sentences.en: You saw it from Chris Murphy, who's in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到身在参议院的克里斯·墨菲的表态。

sentences.en: You can see how tired I am.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出我有多累。

sentences.en: I've been here all weekend.
sentences.zh: 我整个周末都待在这里。

sentences.en: I've been working throughout the past few weeks to try to prevent this moment.
sentences.zh: 过去几周我一直在努力工作，试图阻止这一时刻的发生。

sentences.en: He said we could have won this fight.
sentences.zh: 他说我们本可以赢得这场斗争。

sentences.en: We gave up too early.
sentences.zh: 我们放弃得太早了。

sentences.en: There's no way to defend this.
sentences.zh: 这根本无法辩护。

sentences.en: And you are right to be angry about it.
sentences.zh: 你对此感到愤怒是正确的。

sentences.en: I'm angry about it.
sentences.zh: 我也感到愤怒。

sentences.en: You saw it from Ro Khanna.
sentences.zh: 你看到了罗·卡纳的表态。

sentences.en: Can we recover?
sentences.zh: 我们能恢复过来吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 能。

sentences.en: I think that the first step to recovering is to have generational change and new leadership.
sentences.zh: 我认为恢复的第一步是实现代际更迭和新领导层。

sentences.en: A congressman from California who said Schumer, it's time for him to go.
sentences.zh: 一位来自加利福尼亚州的众议员说，是时候让舒默下台了。

sentences.en: He is not meeting the moment.
sentences.zh: 他已经跟不上时代的需求了。

sentences.en: He's out of touch with where the party's base is.
sentences.zh: 他与党内基层的诉求脱节了。

sentences.en: If you are thinking or planning to run for president as a Democrat in 2028, you've basically denounced this deal.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在考虑或计划以民主党人身份参加2028年总统竞选，你基本上就已经公开谴责了这个协议。

sentences.en: Well, Shane, since Ro Khanna brought Chuck Schumer up, let's talk about his place in all of this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，谢恩，既然罗·卡纳提到了查克·舒默，那我们就来谈谈他在这一切中的地位。

sentences.en: There's a fair bit of anger being directed at him today as we're speaking.
sentences.zh: 正如我们现在所说的那样，有相当一部分愤怒正指向他。

sentences.en: Yet he's the one who brought the Democrats into the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 然而正是他把民主党人带入了政府停摆。

sentences.en: He helped create the strategy.
sentences.zh: 他协助制定了这一策略。

sentences.en: He is the architect of now what has been the longest shutdown in history.
sentences.zh: 他现在是有史以来持续时间最长的政府停摆的始作俑者。

sentences.en: And the architect of fighting on these particular issues.
sentences.zh: 也是围绕这些特定议题进行斗争的幕后推手。

sentences.en: Saying these are something that we can fight for now and win on later.
sentences.zh: 声称这些是我们现在可以争取并在未来赢得胜利的事情。

sentences.en: Elevate this for voters.
sentences.zh: 向选民推高这些议题。

sentences.en: Make them think about affordability.
sentences.zh: 让他们思考负担能力问题。

sentences.en: Make them think about health care.
sentences.zh: 让他们思考医保问题。

sentences.en: He created the message.
sentences.zh: 他创立了这个信息传达策略。

sentences.en: He's kept them on the message.
sentences.zh: 他让大家紧紧围绕这个信息。

sentences.en: And he kept his conference together for 40 days.
sentences.zh: 并且他让他的党团保持团结长达40天。

sentences.en: So why are people mad at him?
sentences.zh: 那为什么人们还在生他的气？

sentences.en: Because he's the leader, right?
sentences.zh: 因为他是领袖，对吧？

sentences.en: The frustration is Chuck Schumer, if he was really the leader, would keep his party in line until he decided that the fact that he didn't vote with them.
sentences.zh: 这种沮丧在于，查克·舒默如果真的是个领袖，本应管好自己的党，直到他决定……其实他没有跟他们一起投票。

sentences.en: Sure, that means he's not supporting ending the shutdown right now.
sentences.zh: 当然，这意味着他并不支持现在就结束政府停摆。

sentences.en: But he's not actually leading and keeping them in line sufficiently to have the fight that they want to have.
sentences.zh: 但他的领导力度和管束能力实际上还不足以引发他们想要的那场大战。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So I just want to observe where we are.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想看看我们目前的处境。

sentences.en: And it's a really interesting place.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的时机。

sentences.en: Democrats who want to be president are railing against this deal that was achieved by fellow Democrats.
sentences.zh: 想要竞选总统的民主党人正在猛烈抨击这份由同党议员达成的协议。

sentences.en: That's how much they want a fight right now against President Trump.
sentences.zh: 这说明他们现在有多渴望与特朗普总统大干一场。

sentences.en: Senators like John Ossoff in a very purple place.
sentences.zh: 像约翰·奥索夫这样身处关键摇摆选区的参议员。

sentences.en: They're fighting this deal to end the shutdown the way that it's probably going to be ending.
sentences.zh: 他们正在全力反对这份可能将以这种方式结束关门的协议。

sentences.en: That's how much he wants a fight against President Trump right now.
sentences.zh: 这说明他现在有多渴望与特朗普总统对抗。

sentences.en: The majority of Senate Democrats are voting against this deal struck by their own fellow Democrats.
sentences.zh: 大多数参议院民主党人都在投票反对由他们同党议员达成的这项协议。

sentences.en: That's how much the whole party wants to be fighting President Trump right now as a kind of a brand message.
sentences.zh: 这表明整个党派现在多么希望将对抗特朗普总统作为一种品牌形象。

sentences.en: And that brings me back to what our colleague Carl Hulse said to me the night that the shutdown began 40-something days ago.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了我们的同事卡尔·赫尔斯在四十多天前政府关门开始的那天晚上对我说的话。

sentences.en: He argued that the Trump era has fundamentally changed the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 他认为，特朗普时代已经从根本上改变了民主党。

sentences.en: In a sense, it's radicalized it.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，它让党派变得更加激进。

sentences.en: And the party wants to say as loudly as possible, we are not the Democratic Party of those eight moderates who did this deal.
sentences.zh: 民主党人想要尽可能大声地宣布：我们不是达成这项协议的那八位温和派代表的民主党。

sentences.en: That's not who we are.
sentences.zh: 那不是我们的本质。

sentences.en: We exist to fight President Trump.
sentences.zh: 我们的存在就是为了对抗特朗普总统。

sentences.en: And if that means we have to fight ourselves in a kind of civil war, if that means we're going to take out our anger at our own Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, so be it.
sentences.zh: 如果这意味着我们必须在一场类似内战的冲突中进行自我内讧，如果这意味着我们要把对参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默的怒火发泄出来，那就这样吧。

sentences.en: We will be the party of fighting Trump, period.
sentences.zh: 我们将坚定不移地成为一个对抗特朗普的政党，就这样。

sentences.en: One of the defining forces for Democrats in Trump's second term is that voters are angry at their own party.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普的第二个任期内，定义民主党的一大核心力量是选民对他们自己的党派感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And I think that's part of what gets us into the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是导致政府关门的原因之一。

sentences.en: It's part of why they're going to be disappointed by the results of the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们对关门结果感到失望的部分原因。

sentences.en: And we're going to see what that looks like next year.
sentences.zh: 我们将拭目以待明年会发生什么。

sentences.en: That anger, that energy, that has worked for parties before to take back power.
sentences.zh: 这种愤怒、这种能量，过去曾帮政党夺回过权力。

sentences.en: And so I think Democrats are trying to tread carefully here.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为民主党人在这里正试图小心翼翼地行事。

sentences.en: They want to keep the voters angry, but they would like to direct the anger at the other party.
sentences.zh: 他们想保持选民的愤怒，但又希望把这种愤怒引导到另一个政党身上。

sentences.en: At the moment, it's being directed internally.
sentences.zh: 目前，这种怒火正指向党内。

sentences.en: And that's getting back to that self-owned moment, right?
sentences.zh: 这就回到了那个自食其果的时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is, last week, you saw angry voters turn out and vote out Republicans all across the country.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，上周你看到愤怒的选民纷纷涌向投票站，把全国各地的共和党人投票赶出了办公室。

sentences.en: And the concern is, what if we've turned that anger back at us now?
sentences.zh: 而大家担心的是，如果我们现在把这种愤怒转向我们自己怎么办？

sentences.en: And as quickly as possible, they're going to try to harness that energy, that anger, that frustration, and say,
sentences.zh: 他们会以最快的速度试图驾驭这股能量、愤怒和挫败感，并宣称：

sentences.en: we fought the good fight here, you wanted us to fight, we did the fight.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里打了一场漂亮的仗，你们希望我们抗争，我们抗争了。

sentences.en: And even if we didn't get everything we wanted, we showed you that we can and would,
sentences.zh: 即使我们没有得到想要的一切，我们也向你们证明了我们能够而且愿意去抗争，

sentences.en: and that the details of how this ended are going to be forgotten far sooner than the fact that they had the fight in the first place.
sentences.zh: 而且这件事如何收场的细节，很快就会被人遗忘，人们记住的只会是他们当初确实抗争过这一事实。

sentences.en: In other words, the message now is, don't worry about the way this ended.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，现在的口号是：不要在意这一切是如何结束的。

sentences.en: Just be glad it even happened.
sentences.zh: 只要庆幸它发生了就好。

sentences.en: Just remember the fight we had.
sentences.zh: 只要记住我们打过的那场仗就行。

sentences.en: Well, Shane, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢恩，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: On Monday night, the Senate approved a package of spending bills, backed by the eight Senate Democrats and every Senate Republican, that would end the government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 周一晚上，参议院批准了一揽子支出法案，该法案得到了八位参议院民主党人和全体共和党人的支持，这将结束政府关门。

sentences.en: Those bills now head to the Republican-controlled House, which is expected to adopt them later this week.
sentences.zh: 这些法案现在将提交给由共和党控制的众议院，预计众议院将在本周晚些时候通过这些法案。

sentences.en: If that happens, the government will reopen by the end of the week.
sentences.zh: 如果情况属实，政府将在本周末前重新开门。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 我是威纳卢。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: At the Supreme Court on Monday, the justices denied a request that they consider overturning the court's landmark 2015 decision to legalize same-sex marriage.
sentences.zh: 在周一的最高法院，大法官们驳回了一项要求他们考虑推翻该法院 2015 年将同性婚姻合法化的里程碑式判决的请求。

sentences.en: The decision was closely watched by gay Americans and their allies,
sentences.zh: 这一决定受到美国同性恋群体及其盟友的密切关注，

sentences.en: who feared that the court's conservative majority might reverse the gay marriage ruling in the same way that they eliminated the nationwide right to an abortion.
sentences.zh: 他们担心最高法院的保守派多数可能会推翻同性婚姻裁决，就像他们取消全国堕胎权那样。

sentences.en: But the high court agreed that it would hear a case challenging mail-in ballot rules across the country.
sentences.zh: 但最高法院同意审理一项对全国各地邮寄选票规则提出挑战的案件。

sentences.en: The case revolves around Mississippi's five-day grace period, which allows election officials to count ballots that have been mailed on election day but arrive a few days later.
sentences.zh: 该案围绕密西西比州的五天宽限期展开，该规定允许选举官员统计在选举日当天寄出但几天后才送达的选票。

sentences.en: Dozens of states have similar grace periods as Mississippi's.
sentences.zh: 几十个州都有与密西西比州相似的宽限期。

sentences.en: So if the court finds that Mississippi's rules are illegal, it could create chaos leading up to the 2026 elections.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果法院裁定密西西比州的规则违法，可能会在 2026 年选举来临之际引发混乱。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种对光线极度敏感、需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会喝到断片来睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean what kind of light do they require because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 我是指他们对光线有什么具体要求，因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
